title: African Languages AI Safety Readiness Report
abstract: arXiv:2610.27269v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: With the widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) across languages and domains, AI safety has emerged as a critical global concern. However, due to resource constraints, research and development efforts tend to prioritize a limited number of high-resource languages, leaving many others, especially those spoken in Africa, underrepresented. While existing research on language "resource-ness" has largely examined whether sufficient resources are available to develop language technologies, the question of whether languages are adequately represented in AI safety research has received attention only more recently. This report examines the readiness of African languages for inclusion in AI safety discussions, drawing on existing literature and data. It considers four factors: the availability of AI-relevant resources, including text data; national AI policy support; performance on established text benchmarks; and speaker population.

translated_title: 非洲语言人工智能安全就绪度报告
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLMs）在各语言和领域的广泛应用，人工智能安全已成为全球关注的关键问题。然而，由于资源限制，研发工作往往优先考虑少数高资源语言，导致许多其他语言，尤其是非洲使用的语言，代表性不足。虽然现有关于语言“资源性”的研究主要考察是否有足够的资源来开发语言技术，但语言在人工智能安全研究中是否得到充分代表的问题直到最近才受到关注。本报告基于现有文献和数据，考察了非洲语言参与人工智能安全讨论的就绪度。报告考虑了四个因素：包括文本数据在内的AI相关资源的可用性；国家AI政策支持；在既定文本基准上的表现；以及说话者人口数量。
tldr: 本报告通过考察AI资源可用性、国家AI政策支持、文本基准表现和说话者人口四个因素，评估了非洲语言参与人工智能安全讨论的就绪度。
